title: Hypertension follow-up
raw_text: 54F here for BP follow-up. Home readings 148-156/88-94. No chest pain, dyspnea, headache, or vision change. Taking lisinopril 10 mg daily, misses about one dose weekly. Exam unremarkable. Increase lisinopril to 20 mg daily. BMP in 2 weeks. Continue home log and return in 4 weeks. ER precautions reviewed.

clinical.hpi: 54-year-old woman with above-goal home blood pressure readings and occasional missed lisinopril doses. No symptoms suggesting acute end-organ injury.

patient_facing.what_we_found: Your blood pressure is still higher than the goal. You do not have warning symptoms today.
patient_facing.why_it_matters: Blood pressure that stays high can strain your heart, brain, and kidneys over time.
what_to_do_next: Take 20 mg of lisinopril every day
Keep a daily blood pressure log
Get the ordered blood test in 2 weeks
patient_facing.urgent_warning: Get emergency help for chest pain, severe trouble breathing, sudden weakness, confusion, or a severe new headache.
teach_back: What dose of lisinopril will you take?

title: Viral upper respiratory infection
raw_text: 29M, cough, congestion and sore throat x3 days. Tmax 100.2 at home. COVID test negative yesterday. Lungs clear, O2 98%, no respiratory distress. Likely viral URI. Fluids, rest, acetaminophen PRN. Return if fever >5 days, worsening, SOB, or dehydration.

clinical.hpi: 29-year-old man with three days of mild upper respiratory symptoms, negative home COVID test, and no respiratory distress.
plan: Supportive care with fluids and rest
follow_up: Return for persistent fever, worsening symptoms, breathing difficulty, or dehydration

patient_facing.what_we_found: Your symptoms and exam fit a common viral infection. Your lungs sound clear and your oxygen level is normal.
patient_facing.why_it_matters: Viruses usually improve on their own, and antibiotics do not treat them.
what_to_do_next: Use acetaminophen as directed if needed
patient_facing.urgent_warning: Seek care quickly if breathing becomes hard, you cannot keep fluids down, symptoms rapidly worsen, or fever lasts more than 5 days.
teach_back: What can you do at home?
Which changes should prompt medical care?

title: New type 2 diabetes discussion
raw_text: 46F reviewing labs: A1c 7.8%, fasting glucose 168. Increased thirst, no vomiting or confusion. Discussed new T2DM diagnosis, diet/activity, eye and foot care. Start metformin ER 500 mg with dinner, increase to 1000 mg after 1 week if tolerated. Urine microalbumin ordered. Follow up 3 months.

clinical.hpi: 46-year-old woman with increased thirst, A1c 7.8%, and fasting glucose 168 mg/dL. No symptoms of acute metabolic decompensation.

patient_facing.what_we_found: Your blood sugar has been high enough to diagnose type 2 diabetes.
patient_facing.why_it_matters: Managing blood sugar protects your eyes, kidneys, nerves, and heart.
what_to_do_next: Take metformin ER 500 mg with dinner
After one week, increase to 1000 mg if your stomach tolerates it
Plan an eye exam and check your feet regularly
patient_facing.urgent_warning: Get urgent help for repeated vomiting, severe weakness, confusion, or trouble staying awake.
teach_back: Which routine checks help prevent complications?
